rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 <U+2013> the authors run 688 LPJmL simulations of their own (water management scenarios, climate change). Q2: Section 2.1.4 and 3.2, Fig 5 <U+2013> irrigation transition scenarios replace surface systems with sprinkler and drip ('best practice': drip where suitable; 'all drip'); simulated consumptive losses on irrigated land are cut by 24, 48 and 85% and global withdrawal falls from 2507 to 2071/1248/808 km3; Section 3.6 compares simulated withdrawal/consumption with FAO and other estimates and simulated yield gains with case-study observations. Q4: Section 3.1<U+2013>3.2, Fig 1 and Fig 5 <U+2013> the model explicitly partitions water into soil evaporation, interception, conveyance losses and transpiration and reports the transpiration coefficient rising from 42% to 49/54/61%. Q5: Fig 2, Fig 3(a), Fig 5(b), Section 3.6 <U+2013> results reported at basin level across the globe for 12 crop types, with named regions (Middle East, central Asia, China, Australia, southern Africa, Americas, flat potentials in SSA). Q6: Sections 3.1<U+2013>3.3, Table 3 <U+2013> effects reported at basin and global scale. Q8: Section 2.1.5 and 3.6 <U+2013> 'max'/'all drip' scenarios are stated to represent biophysical limits not feasible targets; nutrient limitation not represented; adoption levels hard to quantify; groundwater and diversion contributions not quantified; local feasibility beyond scope.
rows.notes: Caveats on Q2: this is a global model; drip is simulated jointly with sprinkler in the 'best practice' scenario and water-saving figures in the text also include SMC on irrigated land (IRR-only bars are shown in Fig 5a); the evaluation against observations in Section 3.6 concerns baseline withdrawals and WH/SMC yield gains rather than drip-specific savings, so Q2 is a qualified yes. Q3: single modeling approach. Q7: drip applicability by crop suitability is an assumption, and the flat SSA potential (only 5% irrigated) explains variation but is not stated as a requirement. Q9: the water-saving results are single values; the 20-GCM ensemble is only reported as medians/averages (Table 4) without dispersion, and Fig S2 is a sensitivity analysis only.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 <U+2013> the study reports its own LPJmL model runs (688 simulations).
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on river flows or aquatic ecosystems. It shows reduced irrigation withdrawal and consumptive losses under drip/sprinkler transitions (Section 3.2, Table 3), which is only a precondition for enhanced river flows; in fact it notes that upstream irrigation and water-harvesting interventions can reduce return flows and downstream water availability (Section 3.6), and the mention of respecting environmental flow requirements (Discussion) is a recommendation, not a finding.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Table 2 <U+2013> own LPJmL simulations (688 runs). Q2: Section 3.3 and Fig 5(b) <U+2013> irrigation improvements (sprinkler/drip transitions) with saved water rerouted to expand irrigation increase global kcal production by 7, 26 and 43% in the 'low', 'ambitious' and 'max' scenarios; Abstract states the 26% figure for the 'ambitious' scenario; Section 2.2 calibrates yields to FAO statistics and Section 3.6 compares simulated yield gains with documented case-study gains. Q4: Sections 3.2<U+2013>3.3, Table 3 <U+2013> the pathway is modeled: consumptive losses cut by 24/48/85%, enabling 90/345/597 Mha expansion, with irrigated area rising from 297 to 642 Mha in the 'ambitious' scenario. Q5: Fig 3(a), Fig 5(b), Section 3.3 and 3.6 <U+2013> basin-level results across the globe and 12 crop types, with regions named (Middle East, Asia, Central/North America) and flat potentials in SSA. Q6: Sections 3.1<U+2013>3.3, Fig 5(b), Table 3 <U+2013> production gains reported at basin and global scales. Q7: Section 3.3 and 2.1.4 <U+2013> expansion gains require available rainfed cropland within the same basin; the authors find some basins lack sufficient rainfed cropland so not all saved water can be used. Q8: Sections 2.1.5, 3.6 <U+2013> 'max'/'all drip' scenario not a feasible target; nutrient limitation not modeled; current adoption of measures unknown; groundwater and transboundary contributions unquantified; local feasibility beyond scope.
rows.notes: Q2 is a qualified yes: results are from a global model whose outputs are checked only partially against observations (FAO yield calibration, comparison of WH/SI yield gains and withdrawals with case studies and other estimates); drip is not isolated from sprinkler in the 'ambitious' scenario and the 26% figure combines irrigation improvement with expansion. Q3: single modeling method. Q9: the 26% result is a single value with no dispersion; the 20-GCM climate ensemble is reported only as averages/medians in Table 4, and Fig S2 is a sensitivity analysis.

notes: Global process-based modeling study (LPJmL) of irrigation improvement (sprinkler/drip), water harvesting and soil moisture conservation under current and 20-GCM future climates; no field measurements of its own. Supplementary figures (S1<U+2013>S5, Table S1<U+2013>S2) and map figures are not included in the text provided.
